about: The differences between the page before the conversion and the React page that have been ruled deliberate. tools/baseline.mjs --compare applies them only when the page it loaded is the React page (it has the #root element), never when it is legacy.html or any other copy of the old page. Each entry names the field it touches, the states it applies to, the old form and the new form, and the ruling with its date. Each is carried out by the rewrite named in 'rewrite', written in tools/baseline.mjs (applyAccepted), which first checks that the old form is really there and fails the state if it is not, so an entry can never absorb a difference it does not describe. Everything an entry does not name is compared exactly as before. Written 2026-09-24, step 5 of docs/CONVERSION_PLAN.md. Add an entry only on a ruling, and say in the commit which ruling.

differences.field: The first column of every table under a chart (the chart name in the ladder's and the feed range chart's tables, the limit in the cascade's table, the speed band in the drill speed chart's table): the cell in results and diagnostics blocks, and the same cell's text in the section's whole text.
differences.statesNote: Every state that shows a chart table: 48 of the 52 on 2026-09-24. The four without one (the two refusals and the two blocks) have nothing for it to touch.
differences.was: In capitals, from the old table's header styling: "ONSRUD 60-100MW (COMPRESSION)", "CHIP LOAD TARGET".
differences.now: In its own case: "Onsrud 60-100MW (compression)", "Chip load target".
differences.rewrite: The React page's row-header text is put in capitals before comparing (toLocaleUpperCase, as the old page's CSS did), in the cells and in those lines of the section's text, so the words must still be the same letters in the same order. The old side is not touched.
differences.ruling: Claude's ruling, 2026-09-24, on the orchestrator's instruction in step 5: the design system's Table part keeps a row header in its own case on purpose, because capitals destroy unit symbols ("Ra 0.8 µm" painted as "RA 0.8 ΜM"); livetools-design-system docs/DECISIONS.md D58, the row-header clause.

differences.field: The whole text of the results and diagnostics sections: the line under each chart table's fold summary.
differences.was: A line holding the table's name ("Every published chart for this cut"), read from the old table's visually hidden caption.
differences.now: No line. The table is named by an accessible label (aria-label) instead, which is not part of the read text. The name itself is unchanged: the table block's caption field is still compared exactly, read from that label.
differences.rewrite: On the old side, the line directly under each table's summary is removed after checking it equals that table's name.
differences.ruling: The design system's Table part names its table with a label and takes no caption (livetools-design-system docs/DECISIONS.md D58, the name clause), accepted by the orchestrator on 2026-09-24 in step 5.

differences.field: form.fields: the Advanced fold's fields in drilling.
differences.was: Thirteen advanced fields on a page opened from a drilling link: the three drilling reads and ten it never reads.
differences.now: The three drilling reads: SPINDLE POWER, SPINDLE BREAKPOINT, MACHINE MAX FEED.
differences.rewrite: On the old side, the ten fields named in 'remove' are taken out of form.fields after checking each is there exactly once. The three that stay are compared exactly.
differences.ruling: Claude's, 2026-09-24, step 2 (docs/CONVERSION_PLAN.md, "The advanced fields on a drilling link"): a bug in the old page, whose app.js hid the routing-only fields before it had built them, so they showed on a drilling link and not after a switch to drilling.

differences.field: results.blocks[n].ariaRole: the role of a banner that appears after the page has loaded.
differences.was: No role: the old results section announced itself as a whole (aria-live), so its banners carried none.
differences.now: role="alert" on a warning or danger banner and role="status" on a success or info banner, given by the Alert part to a banner mounted after load. Only these two states have clicks, so only here are banners mounted after load.
differences.rewrite: On the old side, each banner named in 'blocks' has its ariaRole changed from null to the role given, after checking it is a banner and its role was null.
differences.ruling: The plan's ruling on the double announcement (Claude's, 2026-09-24), carried out in step 3 (docs/CONVERSION_PLAN.md, "How the results announce themselves to a screen reader").

differences.statesNote: Every routing state whose "Show beta tools" box is unticked: the routing states that do not name the ball nose. A state that names it (the four ball-* states, tool-ball-12.7-mdf-depth-empty and the two ball-nose refusals) opens with the box ticked and the list whole, so this rewrites nothing there; drilling shows the drill list, which never had the ball nose.
differences.was: Five tool types, the last "Ball nose" with its hint.
differences.now: The four flat tools only, while the box is unticked. The ball nose arrived in commit bc85559 and was never live; wood.fusioncam.co serves commit 1e6c265, which had no ball nose.
differences.option:
Ball nose
Round tip for 3D surfacing and carving. Softwood, hardwood and MDF only.
differences.rewrite: Only where the React page's "Show beta tools" box is there and unticked: on the old side, the ball nose option is taken out of the tool list after checking it is there exactly once, last, and not the chosen tool. Listed before beta-checkbox, which removes the box this one reads.
differences.ruling: Scott's ruling, 2026-09-24: the ball nose, the bull nose and 3D surfacing go live behind a beta switch, off by default, and with it off the page offers what the live site offers.

differences.field: form.fields: a checkbox under the tool list.
differences.statesNote: Every routing state (the React page shows the box in routing only). Unticked in all of them except the seven that name the ball nose, where a ball-nose link ticks it.
differences.now: A "Show beta tools" checkbox directly after the material, where the tool list sits, with its hint; ticked exactly when the chosen tool is the ball nose (the baseline runs in a fresh browser, so nothing is remembered).
differences.hint: Adds the ball nose, for 3D surfacing and carving. Its numbers are new and less proven than the rest; start conservatively.
differences.rewrite: On the React side, the one field whose checkbox reads "Show beta tools" is taken out after checking it is there exactly once in a routing state (and not at all in drilling), directly after MATERIAL, with no label of its own, this hint, no message, and ticked exactly when the chosen tool is the ball nose.
differences.ruling: Scott's ruling, 2026-09-24: the beta switch is a checkbox beside the tool type, off by default and remembered in the browser; a link naming the ball nose opens with it ticked.
